threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the Tube' means a quick ride, not an exercise in standing still while the trains sit idle for hours.
Saw a lad serenading a girl with an old Nokia ringtone on the 196 last night. Never thought I’d see a 2000s phone make a comeback, let alone on a night bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a piece of berliner currywurst under my favorite park bench—it's like the neighborhood was welcoming me with its quirks.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find people casually debating the merits of currywurst while sipping craft beer at 9 AM in a park. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name the burrito shop by the smell alone, even through the BART delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 25 bus calmly juggling oranges while chatting about crypto. Only in San Francisco do you get a fruit market on wheels.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the street fiestas are planned—most just erupt spontaneously, fueled by a few tinto de verano and good vibes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look at the Metro map like it's a treasure map, trying to decipher the labyrinth of lines instead of just jumping on the nearest train.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can catch a Tube during rush hour. Good luck! It's like the whole city forgot how to queue.
Last Friday on the 196, a guy started singing ‘Wonderwall’ to a bus full of strangers; by the end, we were all harmonizing. Magic happens on the night bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a family of ducks waddling down Karl-Marx-Straße, completely indifferent to the bustling traffic. It felt like a scene straight from a quirky film.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find cafes with a side of Turkish breakfast and street art on every corner that tells stories from decades of change.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate the BART chaos; they’ve learned to avoid Civic Center like it’s on fire, which, at times, it kinda is.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus yesterday with a guy loudly reading a Yelp review to the driver. About tacos. He nearly missed his stop, but we all laughed.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a cafe con leche on every corner like back home. Here, it’s a serious ritual—don’t rush it!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still asking for the 'barcelona' pronunciation with the soft 'c'—the locals dropped that a long time ago.
